DOMAIN 29 / 36

LOGIKĒ

Logic — the algebra of thought. The lineage that walked logic into mathematics: from Thales of Miletus' first deductive proof (c. 600 BCE — a truth that must be PROVEN, not merely seen), through Aristotle's syllogism, Euclid's axioms and the Stoics' propositions, to Leibniz's dream of calculation and George Boole's algebra of true and false — the direct ancestor of every gate in PSĒPHOS. One logician per sphere, each with a live demonstration of their idea, and each honest about how sure we really are. (λογική, logikē — 'of reasoning', from logos: word, ratio, account.)

39 spheres
THALES OF MILETUS · I
the first to PROVE — a truth that must follow by argument, not merely be observed

THALES OF MILETUS (c. 624–546 BCE) — LOGIKĒ I, the FIRST to walk logic into mathematics. Before him math was RECIPES (Egyptian/Babylonian 'to find the area, do this' — trusted because it works); Thales asked WHY MUST it be so, and answered by ARGUMENT — a chain of reasons true for EVERY case at once. ⚑ LIVE: Thales' Theorem — drag the point P around a semicircle, the inscribed angle ∠APB stays EXACTLY 90° for all P, with the deductive proof made visible (drop the radius OP → two isosceles triangles → base angles α+β=90° ⟹ ∠APB=90°, the 'must' not the 'does'). The five theorems traditionally his (diameter halves the circle; isosceles base angles equal; vertical angles equal; the semicircle right angle; ASA). THE MAN: predicted the solar eclipse of 28 May 585 BCE (it stopped a battle — an oldest precisely-datable event); measured a pyramid by its shadow (similar triangles); 'water is the arche' (first natural philosophy, explaining the world without gods). CONFIDENCE-TIERED (honest about an ancient figure): STRONG (the reputation — Aristotle/Herodotus/Proclus name him founder; the eclipse is astronomically fixed) / TRADITIONAL (the theorems — documented centuries later via Eudemus→Proclus) / DEBATED (whether he 'proved' formally, or deduction matured later and was projected back). ⚑ Gate kept on: Thales LEFT NO SURVIVING WRITING — the romance and the record don't perfectly align, and saying so is the point. Seeds the LOGIKĒ domain; next → [[pythagoras]] (the front of the lineage).

enter ↗code
PYTHAGORAS &amp; THE BROTHERHOOD
the front (c. 570 BCE) — number as reality, and the first proof by contradiction (√2)

PYTHAGORAS &amp; THE BROTHERHOOD (c. 570–495 BCE) — LOGIKĒ, the FRONT (between [[thales-of-miletus]] and [[aristotle]]). Thales proved the first theorem; the Pythagoreans made PROOF a way of life and staked a creed on it: NUMBER — whole numbers and their ratios — is the substance of reality. Real evidence: musical HARMONY is whole-number ratio (octave 2:1, fifth 3:2, fourth 4:3). But their own devotion to proof produced the discovery that BROKE the creed — a clean REDUCTIO AD ABSURDUM that √2 (the diagonal of a unit square) is NO ratio of whole numbers: the first famous proof by contradiction, the deductive engine of all logic. LIVE: (1) step the √2 irrationality proof (assume p/q in lowest terms → p²=2q² → p even → q even → both even → contradicts lowest terms; rational approximations 1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12… crowd √2 but their squares never reach 2, verified); (2) the consonant musical ratios on a string (click to hear the interval). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (√2's irrationality is a real, early proof-by-contradiction; the consonance ratios are real; the cult of proof shaped Greek math) / THE-MAN-IS-A-FOG (Pythagoras wrote nothing; 'Pythagoras' = the brotherhood; the theorem a²+b²=c² was used by Babylonians ~1000 yrs earlier) / MYSTICISM (number-worship, transmigration, secrecy; ⚠ the irrationality result is credited to HIPPASUS, whom legend says the order drowned for revealing it). ⚑ A community devoted to proof followed its own method to a truth it could not bear — the tool stronger than the creed. [[thales-of-miletus]] ← · next → Parmenides.

enter ↗code
PARMENIDES OF ELEA
the front (c. 515 BCE) — reason over the senses; the first rationalist

PARMENIDES OF ELEA (c. 515–450 BCE) — LOGIKĒ, the FRONT, founder of the Eleatic school and the FIRST RATIONALIST. Pythagoras trusted number; Parmenides trusted ARGUMENT ITSELF, even against the plain evidence of the eyes. In a visionary poem he laid down the first sustained PURE DEDUCTION in the Western record: from one premise ('what is, is; what is not cannot be — nor even be thought') he reasoned, step by valid step, that CHANGE, MOTION, and PLURALITY are impossible and that Being is one, eternal, unchanging. He was WRONG — but in following a valid argument off the cliff of common sense he founded rationalism and handed logic its first law: contradiction is the mark of the false. LIVE: a deduction-walker — one premise → no not-being → no void → no coming-to-be → no change → no plurality → Being is One (every arrow valid, the premise the flaw) + the Way of Truth vs the Way of Opinion. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG-the-METHOD (the birth of deduction; reason, not observation, settles what can be; contradiction as a tool — the foundation of logic &amp; math) / FALSE-the-CONCLUSION (⚠ 'change is impossible' is plainly false; the flaw is the premise treating 'nothing' as a thinkable thing — the perfect lesson that a VALID argument can still be UNSOUND) / MYSTIC-NOT-GEOMETER (delivered as a goddess's speech in hexameter; reading it as tidy logic is partly modern reconstruction). ⚑ A false conclusion reached by a valid road — and in walking it he BUILT the road; [[aristotle]] would found validity-theory on exactly his valid/sound distinction. [[pythagoras]] ← · next → Zeno.

enter ↗code
ZENO OF ELEA
the front (c. 490 BCE) — the paradoxes of motion; the first proofs by contradiction & infinity

ZENO OF ELEA (c. 490–430 BCE) — LOGIKĒ, the FRONT, pupil of [[parmenides]] and (per Aristotle) the INVENTOR OF DIALECTIC. To defend his teacher's changeless One, Zeno forged a devastating new weapon — the PARADOX, a proof by contradiction aimed at common sense: grant that space &amp; time are infinitely divisible and MOTION DISSOLVES INTO ABSURDITY. Swift Achilles can never catch a tortoise with a head start (each time he reaches where it was, it has crept further); an arrow in flight is, at each instant, at REST. These were the first arguments to take INFINITY seriously, and they were not truly answered for two thousand years — until the CALCULUS showed an unending sum of shrinking steps can have a FINITE total (½+¼+⅛+…=1). LIVE: run Achilles &amp; the tortoise — watch the infinite stages and the geometric series 1+1/10+1/100+… converge to a finite catch-up point (10/9, verified) + the dichotomy &amp; the arrow. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the first systematic proofs by contradiction; the first serious confrontation with the infinite — problems that drove the rigor of limits) / 'DISSOLVED'-NOT-TRIVIAL (⚠ the convergent-series resolution is COMPLETE &amp; correct, made rigorous by Cauchy/Weierstrass — pop claims 'math can't answer Zeno' are wrong; but the ARROW &amp; supertasks are still genuinely debated) / A-DEFENCE-NOT-A-SYSTEM (polemics protecting Parmenides' One, read mostly second-hand via Aristotle). ⚑ A 'wrong' argument so sharp it helped summon the calculus into being — and the front of the lineage is now whole. [[parmenides]] ← · next → [[aristotle]].

enter ↗code
ARISTOTLE · II
the first SYSTEM of valid inference — the syllogism + the three laws of thought

ARISTOTLE (384–322 BCE) — LOGIKĒ II, the father of formal logic. Thales proved truths one at a time; Aristotle made REASONING ITSELF the object of study: in the Organon he built the first SYSTEM of valid inference — the SYLLOGISM (three terms S/M/P, two premises → a conclusion that CANNOT be false if the premises are true, by FORM not content) — and named the THREE LAWS of thought (identity A=A; non-contradiction ¬(A∧¬A), 'the firmest'; excluded middle A∨¬A). ⚑ LIVE: a syllogism machine — pick the major (M-P) & minor (S-M) premises, it rules VALID/INVALID + the conclusion + an Euler diagram (figure-1 valid moods computed: Barbara AAA, Celarent EAE, Darii AII, Ferio EIO; the rest fail). His logic ruled ~2,000 years — Kant called it finished and perfect. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the syllogism & the laws are foundational and correct) / LIMITED (it's TERM logic — categories only; it cannot express RELATIONS 'Alice taller than Bob' or nested quantifiers, the sentences math runs on) / SUPERSEDED (Frege's predicate logic 1879 blew the roof off; and 'Aristotelian authority' in physics delayed science until Galileo). ⚑ Father of logic, not the last word — the lineage runs from here to the man who finished it. [[thales-of-miletus]] ← · next → Euclid.

enter ↗code
EUCLID · III
the first complete deductive EDIFICE — from 10 axioms, all of geometry

EUCLID (fl. c. 300 BCE, Alexandria) — LOGIKĒ III. Thales proved a truth, Aristotle named the valid forms; Euclid built the CATHEDRAL: in the Elements, from a handful of definitions + 5 POSTULATES + 5 COMMON NOTIONS, he deduced ~465 theorems across 13 books in strict order, each resting only on what was proved before — the first complete AXIOMATIC SYSTEM, and the model of 'rigorous reasoning' for 2,000+ years. ⚑ LIVE: (1) Proposition 1 — the very FIRST proof in the book — step through the equilateral-triangle construction (⊙A ∩ ⊙B → C; AC=AB & BC=AB both radii, so AC=BC=AB by Common Notion 1), drag A/B to see it hold for any segment; (2) the 10 foundations laid out (note P5 is conspicuously longer); (3) THE FIFTH POSTULATE — the parallel postulate — a curvature slider showing a triangle's angle sum: 180° flat, >180° sphere, <180° saddle. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the axiomatic method & the Elements — most influential textbook ever) / GAPPED (not actually airtight — Euclid used unstated assumptions: that the two circles MEET, that points lie 'between'; HILBERT 1899 needed ~20 more axioms to close them) / A CHOICE (the 5th is INDEPENDENT — can't be proved from the rest; deny it → consistent NON-EUCLIDEAN geometries, Bolyai/Lobachevsky/Riemann → the shape of Einstein's universe). ⚑ Gate kept on: 'Euclid' the man is nearly a blank (anecdotes centuries later; possibly a school). The greatest deductive system ever — and proof the gold standard had hidden joints. [[aristotle]] ← · next → the Stoics (propositional logic).

enter ↗code
CHRYSIPPUS & THE STOICS · IV
propositional logic — the truth table & the gate, ~2000 years early

CHRYSIPPUS OF SOLI (c. 279–206 BCE) & the Stoics — LOGIKĒ IV, the PIVOTAL one for computing. Aristotle reasoned about CATEGORIES; the Stoics reasoned about whole STATEMENTS joined by CONNECTIVES — and, or, not, IF…THEN — the first PROPOSITIONAL logic. ⚑ THE BRIDGE TO THE GATE: a proposition is true/false = the BIT; the connectives = the OPERATORS; Philo of Megara's conditional 'if P then Q' is FALSE in exactly one case (P true, Q false) = the MATERIAL CONDITIONAL = the modern TRUTH TABLE, written ~300 BCE (verified 1011). LIVE: (1) toggle P/Q → the connectives compute (¬, ∧, ∨, ⊻, →) + the full 4-row truth table with the current row lit — every box a logic gate 2,200 years before silicon; (2) the FIVE INDEMONSTRABLES (modus ponens 'if P then Q; P; ∴ Q'; modus tollens; conj-denial; excl-disjunction; disjunctive syllogism) — the first natural-deduction rules — lighting up when their premises hold. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (they built propositional logic — connectives, truth-functional conditional, inference rules — the genuine ancestor of Boolean logic & the gate, per Łukasiewicz/Mates/Bobzien) / RECONSTRUCTED (Chrysippus wrote 705 books, NONE survive whole — rebuilt from hostile critics Sextus Empiricus & Diogenes Laertius; the precise truth-functional reading is partly a 20th-c. reconstruction) / VINDICATED LATE (dismissed as inferior to Aristotle for ~2000 years, until propositional logic became the spine of computing). ⚑ A FIRST THAT WAS FORGOTTEN — and turned out the more important one; this is the logic your processor actually runs on. [[euclid]] ← · next → Ramon Llull (the first logic machine).

enter ↗code
RAMON LLULL · V
the first machine of thought — rotating wheels that generate every combination of ideas (~1300)

RAMON LLULL (c. 1232–1316, Majorca) — LOGIKĒ V, the first to MECHANISE reasoning. Everyone before reasoned by hand; Llull built a DEVICE — the Ars Magna's rotating concentric wheels (VOLVELLES) inscribed with concepts, that crank out EVERY combination of those ideas faster than a mind could list them. The first paper machine that PROCESSES rather than records — 3½ centuries before Pascal's gears, and the seed Leibniz grew into the dream of calculating thought. ⚑ LIVE: (1) the volvelle — nine 'dignities' B–K (Goodness/Greatness/Eternity/Power/Wisdom/Will/Virtue/Truth/Glory) on an inner wheel turning inside an outer; drag or spin it, the pointer reads each new pairing; (2) the ars combinatoria — the 9×9 grid, 9 principles → C(9,2)=36 distinct pairs, the machine's full exhaustive output. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the first logic MACHINE — combinatorial generation by rotating disks, genuine & documented; Leibniz explicitly traced his combinatorics to it) / A GENERATOR (it LISTS, doesn't PROVE — produces propositions, not verdicts; purpose was THEOLOGICAL apologetics, more mnemonic/mystical than rigorous; its grand aim of mechanically demonstrating doctrine simply doesn't work) / VINDICATED (the IDEA — mechanise reasoning by combining symbols on a machine — was centuries early and became, via Leibniz, the spine of computing). ⚑ A first not of logic's CONTENT but of its MECHANISATION — the offloading of reasoning onto a device IS the idea of computing. He wrote ~250 works (pioneering literary Catalan), learned Arabic, died stoned on a mission to Tunis (~1316, traditional). [[chrysippus]] ← · next → William of Ockham (the medieval root).

enter ↗code
WILLIAM OF OCKHAM
the medieval root (c. 1320) — Ockham's razor, supposition theory, De Morgan's laws five centuries early

WILLIAM OF OCKHAM (c. 1287–1347) — LOGIKĒ, THE MEDIEVAL ROOT (between [[ramon-llull]] and [[leibniz]] — the gap the lineage had skipped). The Middle Ages didn't sleep on logic; they forged it hard in the universities, and the sharpest mind was this Franciscan friar. He built SUPPOSITION THEORY (a rigorous account of how terms REFER), stated what we now credit to [[augustus-de-morgan]] FIVE CENTURIES EARLY (negating 'A and B' gives 'not-A or not-B'), and argued NOMINALISM (universals like 'redness' are NAMES in the mind, not things in the world). Famous for ⚑ OCKHAM'S RAZOR: do not multiply entities beyond necessity — prefer the simpler adequate explanation — the founding intuition of modern MODEL SELECTION. LIVE: the razor as OVERFITTING — noisy points from a line; raise the polynomial degree and the curve bends through every point (fit error→0) while WIGGLING wildly between them (fitting noise, not signal); the simplest adequate model generalises (least-squares + Lagrange, verified Runge oscillation grows with degree). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (supposition theory & the De Morgan rules are real high-order medieval logic; the razor is sound method science still runs on) / A-HEURISTIC-NOT-A-LAW (⚠ simpler ≠ true; the razor is a TIE-BREAKER for equally-good explanations, not a theorem — reality is sometimes complicated; its modern forms = regularisation, MDL, Bayesian Occam) / THE-WORDING-IS-LATER (⚠ 'entia non sunt multiplicanda' is a 17th-c. paraphrase; Ockham used the idea, not that Latin slogan). The man: summoned to Avignon for heresy, broke with the Pope over apostolic poverty, fled to the Emperor, excommunicated, died in exile (likely the Black Death). ⚑ The friar who told the future to keep it simple. [[ramon-llull]] ← · next → Leibniz.

enter ↗code
LEIBNIZ · VI
the hinge — 'Calculemus!' · reasoning reduced to calculation; binary + logic-as-arithmetic

GOTTFRIED LEIBNIZ (1646–1716) — LOGIKĒ VI, the HINGE between Llull's wheel and Boole's algebra. Llull combined ideas; Leibniz dreamed the whole machine: a UNIVERSAL SYMBOLIC LANGUAGE (characteristica universalis) + a CALCULUS OF REASONING (calculus ratiocinator), so two people who disagree would not argue but compute — 'CALCULEMUS!', settle it like a sum. ⚑ LIVE: (1) BINARY — toggle 8 bits → any number as a pattern of 0/1 (the register, the only thing a gate can read; he formalised base-2 in 1703, 250 yrs before the machines); (2) 'CALCULEMUS' MADE LITERAL — his actual 1679 idea: give each attribute a PRIME, let a concept be the PRODUCT of its attributes' primes, and a syllogism becomes a DIVISION (man = animal×rational = 2×3 = 6; 'all men are animal?' ⟺ 2 divides 6 = VALID; build the concept, watch inferences settle by arithmetic — verified). He built the four-operation Stepped Reckoner; our calculus notation dx, ∫ is his (despite the Newton priority war). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (binary, the engine, and 'Calculemus!' the vision all computing pursues) / UNFINISHED (the characteristica & calculus were a lifelong PROGRAM never completed; his logical algebra sat UNPUBLISHED ~200 yrs, so Boole re-found it independently) / IMPOSSIBLE-IN-FULL (⚑ the deepest twist — Gödel 1931 & Turing 1936 proved NO method decides EVERY truth by calculation; reasoning CAN be mechanised — that half runs on your desk — but not completely; Leibniz got the direction exactly right and the limit exactly wrong). [[ramon-llull]] ← · next → George Boole.

enter ↗code
GEORGE BOOLE · VII
the destination — logic becomes an algebra of 0 and 1; AND is ×, NOT is 1−x · the gate's ancestor

GEORGE BOOLE (1815–1864) — LOGIKĒ VII, the DESTINATION. Leibniz dreamed logic could be algebra; Boole — a shoemaker's son, self-taught — simply DID IT. Let 1=true, 0=false, and the laws of reasoning become an ALGEBRA: ⚑ AND is MULTIPLICATION (x·y), OR is ADDITION (x+y−xy), NOT is 1−x — reasoning carried out as a SUM (The Laws of Thought, 1854). The single law that makes it logic not arithmetic: x²=x — true only for 0 and 1, so every variable is forced true/false; its twin x(1−x)=0 IS Aristotle's non-contradiction, now a quadratic. ⚑ THE BRIDGE TO THE GATE: in 1937 SHANNON saw a switch is also a 0/1 — series = AND, parallel = OR — so Boolean algebra is the blueprint of every digital circuit. LIVE: (1) toggle x/y → the four ops compute as arithmetic = the truth table (AND=xy verified 1000, OR 1110, XOR 0110); (2) x²=x — y=x and y=x² meet ONLY at 0,1 (verified); (3) a switch circuit — flip A/B, series/parallel, the lamp obeys Boole's arithmetic. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (logic IS algebra — AND=×, NOT=1−x, x²=x — exact & foundational, via Shannon the literal basis of every gate) / REFINED-LATER (Boole's OWN 1854 system was quirky — uninterpretable 2x, division; Jevons/Peirce/Schröder filed it to the idempotent lattice x+x=x) / COMPLETED-BY-OTHERS (propositional/class logic only, no quantifiers/relations → Frege next; the circuit link is Shannon's, 70 yrs on; Boole never touched a circuit). Died at 49 (pneumonia, after walking miles in rain to lecture); an 'ingenious curiosity' in life, revealed a century later as the man who wrote the grammar of the machine age. ⚑ The lineage ARRIVES — Boole's algebra is what runs in [[the-branch-predictor]] & all of PSĒPHOS. [[leibniz]] ← · next → De Morgan / Frege / Shannon.

enter ↗code
AUGUSTUS DE MORGAN · VIII
the duality — negation swaps ∧ and ∨; why one NAND gate builds everything

AUGUSTUS DE MORGAN (1806–1871) — LOGIKĒ VIII, Boole's friend & champion. Boole gave logic an algebra; De Morgan gave it the symmetry every engineer leans on: ⚑ DE MORGAN'S LAWS — negation SWAPS AND and OR: ¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B and ¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B (to deny BOTH is to assert EITHER-NOT; verified all 4 rows). ⚑ WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GATE: this duality is exactly why a single NAND (or NOR) gate is UNIVERSAL — NOT=NAND(A,A), AND=¬(NAND), OR=¬(¬A∧¬B)=pure De Morgan — so a chip is a sea of one gate tiled billions of times (verified: NAND builds NOT/AND/OR matching the real gates). LIVE: (1) toggle A/B → both laws hold + a VENN (the region outside the overlap IS the union of the two outsides); (2) NAND universality — the basic gates built from NAND alone, each matching its real counterpart. He also pushed past Aristotle into the LOGIC OF RELATIONS ('every head of a horse is a head of an animal' — term logic couldn't) → the crack Frege opened. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the laws are bedrock; via NAND/NOR universality the daily workhorse of digital design) / OLDER-THAN-HIM (the name is honorific — Ockham & Buridan stated them in the 1300s, implicit in the Stoics; De Morgan NAMED & ALGEBRAISED them in the new symbolic logic) / A-POINTER (his relational logic broke Aristotle's ceiling but was incomplete — Peirce & Frege built the real predicate logic). First maths professor at UCL (resigned TWICE on principle), coined 'mathematical induction', wrote A Budget of Paradoxes, was x years old in year x² (43 in 1849). [[george-boole]] ← · next → Jevons (the Logic Piano).

enter ↗code
WILLIAM STANLEY JEVONS
the Boolean cleanup (1866) — the LOGIC PIANO, the first machine to solve formal logic

WILLIAM STANLEY JEVONS (1835–1882) — LOGIKĒ, the BOOLEAN CLEANUP (alongside [[george-boole]]/[[augustus-de-morgan]]). Boole's algebra was quirky (uninterpretable terms, exclusive 'or', meaningless division); Jevons CLEANED IT UP — made 'or' INCLUSIVE, enshrined the idempotent law x+x=x, and recast inference as ELIMINATION over a 'logical alphabet' of every term-combination. Then he built ⚑ THE LOGIC PIANO (1866) — a wooden keyboard machine that takes premises and, by knocking out every combination they forbid, DISPLAYS the valid conclusions on its face: the FIRST machine ever to solve a problem of formal logic, a Boolean computer 70 years before electronics (it survives in Oxford's museum). LIVE: play the Logic Piano — the 8 term-combinations (A,B,C) as keys; toggle premises and watch contradictory worlds go dark; the survivors ARE the conclusion (verified: All A→B + All B→C derives All A→C, Barbara, mechanically). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (a real working logic machine + a sound cleanup of Boole — inclusive OR, idempotency, elimination) / A-DEMONSTRATOR (handles a few terms — proves logic CAN be machined, not a general computer; the Boolean-algebra=switching-circuits leap is [[claude-shannon]]'s, 70 yrs on) / LOGIC-WAS-HIS-SIDELINE (better known as an ECONOMIST — co-founder of the marginal-utility revolution, namesake of the 'Jevons paradox'; drowned swimming at 46). ⚑ The first time inference left the human head and entered a device — the gate, in its first wooden draft. [[augustus-de-morgan]] ← · next → John Venn.

enter ↗code
JOHN VENN
the visual logic (1880) — the Venn diagram: a logical statement you can SEE

JOHN VENN (1834–1923) — LOGIKĒ, the VISUAL LOGIC. Boole & Jevons made logic a matter of combinations; Venn made those combinations something you can SEE. ⚑ THE VENN DIAGRAM (1880): overlapping circles divide the plane into REGIONS, one per combination of in/out (in A&B not C; in all three; in none) — so a logical statement becomes a PATTERN OF SHADING ('no A are B' = blacken the A∩B lens) and a syllogism becomes a PICTURE: shade what the premises forbid, read the conclusion off what's left. The most successful NOTATION in the history of logic — the one diagram that escaped the seminar room onto every whiteboard. LIVE: a 3-set Venn — toggle categorical premises, watch regions shade empty (red), the survivors & the A–C conclusion read off the picture (verified All A→B + All B→C shows All A→C). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (a SOUND, COMPLETE visual method for class logic — every region a real combination, validity literally visible; arguably the most-recognised object in all of math) / EULER-CAME-FIRST (⚠ Leonhard Euler drew logical circles a century earlier; Venn's innovation = always draw ALL regions then SHADE, so the diagram can represent ignorance — he called them improved 'Eulerian circles') / BREAKS-DOWN-PAST-3–4-SETS (gorgeous for 2–3 classes, awkward at 4 (ellipses), unreadable beyond — the eye is not a general computer). ⚑ The 8 regions of a 3-circle diagram ARE the 8 rows of a 3-variable truth table = [[william-stanley-jevons]]'s 8 piano keys = a Karnaugh map; shade-to-eliminate is how circuit engineers still simplify gates. Also a frequency-probabilist; built a cricket bowling-machine that clean-bowled an Australian star. The truth table you can look at. [[william-stanley-jevons]] ← · next → Ernst Schröder (the algebra finished).

enter ↗code
ERNST SCHRÖDER
the Boolean cleanup (1890–1905) — the canonical Algebra of Logic; the lattice axioms &amp; duality

ERNST SCHRÖDER (1841–1902) — LOGIKĒ, the BOOLEAN CLEANUP. By the 1880s the algebra of logic was a brilliant mess (Boole started it, Jevons tidied it, Peirce deepened it with relations) scattered across clashing papers. Schröder built the CATHEDRAL: the three-volume VORLESUNGEN ÜBER DIE ALGEBRA DER LOGIK (1890–1905) gathered it all into one rigorous structure — the canonical laws of MEET (∧), JOIN (∨), and COMPLEMENT, the principle of DUALITY (swap ∧↔∨ and 0↔1 and every theorem still holds), recognisable today as a BOOLEAN ALGEBRA / LATTICE. He turned Boole's insight into a finished branch of mathematics. LIVE: the Boolean lattice on the subsets of {a,b,c} (8 nodes by inclusion) — click two nodes, see their meet & join; the axioms hold (distributive + absorption verified, a Boolean algebra; self-dual). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the definitive synthesis of Boolean algebra & the calculus of relations + duality; the standard reference for decades) / CONSOLIDATOR-NOT-ORIGINATOR (the core ideas are Boole's/Peirce's/Jevons's; his genius was completeness & rigour — and the algebraic tradition he perfected was about to be eclipsed by [[gottlob-frege]]'s quantificational logic) / A-SECOND-CLAIM (the SCHRÖDER–BERNSTEIN theorem in set theory bears his name — his proof had a gap, Bernstein fixed it). ⚑ He perfected the algebra of logic just as Frege overshadowed it for foundations — but the EQUATIONAL view he finished is exactly the one that came roaring back through [[claude-shannon]] into computer science. The completed algebra running in [[psephos-processors-domain]]. [[john-venn]] ← · next → the modern foundations.

enter ↗code
GOTTLOB FREGE · IX
the greatest leap since Aristotle — quantifiers ∀/∃, relations, predicate logic (1879)

GOTTLOB FREGE (1848–1925) — LOGIKĒ IX, the founder of MODERN logic, the biggest advance since Aristotle. For 2,000 years logic could say 'all men are mortal' but NOT 'every number has a larger one' — the missing piece was QUANTITY. In the Begriffsschrift (1879) Frege supplied it: ⚑ QUANTIFIERS (∀ 'for all', ∃ 'there exists'), BOUND VARIABLES, and the analysis of a statement as a FUNCTION of arguments (Mortal(Socrates), not subject-predicate) — so logic could finally express the sentences of mathematics, and later the queries of a database & the types of a program. This is FIRST-ORDER (predicate) logic. LIVE: (1) ∀x/∃x over a clickable domain of red/blue objects (the thing term logic couldn't do — quantifiers + connectives, incl. the tautology ∀x(Red∨Blue) & contradiction ∃x(Red∧Blue)); (2) RELATIONS — a clickable R(x,y) matrix where ∀x∃y ('everyone relates to someone', true) ≠ ∃y∀x ('someone everyone relates to', false) — same symbols, swapped order, different claim (verified); (3) the RUSSELL PARADOX — 'the set of all sets that don't contain themselves: is R∈R?' → contradiction either way (clickable), the letter that wrecked his life's work in 1902. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (predicate logic/quantifiers — foundational & permanent, THE logic of modern math & CS) / COLLAPSED (his LOGICISM — math = pure logic — destroyed by Russell's paradox as Grundgesetze vol.2 was at the printer; refounded later on type theory/ZFC) / IGNORED-THEN-OWNED (almost unread in life — flows down only via Russell/Wittgenstein/Carnap; ⚠ HONEST: his 1924 diaries record virulent antisemitic & anti-democratic views — the logic stands, the man does not). [[augustus-de-morgan]] ← · next → Kurt Gödel (the limits).

enter ↗code
KURT GÖDEL · X
the limits — true statements no system can prove; numbering = code as data (1931)

KURT GÖDEL (1906–1978) — LOGIKĒ X, the limit of the whole dream. Leibniz wanted a calculus that settles every question; Hilbert turned it into a PROGRAM — one complete, consistent, mechanical system proving all of mathematics. In 1931, at twenty-five, Gödel proved it can NEVER exist. ⚑ THE TWO INCOMPLETENESS THEOREMS: (1) any consistent formal system strong enough for arithmetic contains TRUE statements it cannot PROVE — truth outruns proof; (2) such a system can never prove its OWN consistency — no foundation certifies itself from inside. ⚑ THE METHOD that did it — GÖDEL NUMBERING: give each symbol a code, encode a whole formula as ∏ primeᵢ^codeᵢ (Leibniz's prime trick made rigorous), so by unique factorisation every statement IS a number → arithmetic can talk about itself → he built the sentence G that says 'G is not provable'. If consistent, G is true but unprovable. ⚑ That same move — a statement is a number, code is data — is the seed of the stored-program computer; five years on Turing recast the diagonal as the HALTING PROBLEM. LIVE: (1) Gödel numbering — build a formula, watch it become a single integer via primes (BigInt, 0=0 → 270 verified); (2) the self-referential sentence — choose 'suppose it proves G' (→ proves a falsehood → inconsistent) or 'suppose it can't' (→ G is true & unprovable → incompleteness); both doors corner the system. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the theorems are proven, rigorous, among the summits of mathematics) / LIMITED-SCOPE (they bound CONSISTENT systems strong enough for ARITHMETIC and concern FORMAL PROVABILITY only — they do NOT say math is broken or nothing is certain; the Gödel sentence is in fact TRUE, just unprovable inside) / MOST-MISQUOTED (⚠ HONEST: the most abused theorem in history — invoked for relativism, 'no absolute truth', theology, consciousness; almost all such uses are wrong). The man: escaped Austria via the Trans-Siberian railway, Einstein's daily walking companion at Princeton, found a supposed dictatorship-loophole in the U.S. Constitution at his citizenship hearing; gripped by a paranoid fear of poisoning he ate only what his wife prepared, and when she was hospitalised in 1977 he stopped eating, dying of starvation at 71 — the prover of certainty's limits undone by an excess of doubt. ⚑ The dream that began at [[leibniz]] meets its ceiling; reasoning can be mechanised — that became PSĒPHOS — but never completed. [[gottlob-frege]] ← · next → Alan Turing (the machine).

enter ↗code
ALAN TURING · XI
the machine — computation defined, the universal computer, the halting limit (1936)

ALAN TURING (1912–1954) — LOGIKĒ XI, the man who gave logic a MACHINE. Gödel proved the formal dream had a ceiling; Turing, 23, asked what 'mechanically computable' even MEANS and answered with a device so simple it defines the word: ⚑ THE TURING MACHINE — a HEAD on an infinite TAPE of 0/1 cells, a STATE, and a tiny RULE TABLE ('in this state reading this symbol → write, move L/R, change state'). Nothing else — and it can compute anything computable at all ('On Computable Numbers', 1936). ⚑ THE UNIVERSAL MACHINE: one Turing machine can read the description of ANY other off its tape and simulate it → hardware & program become SEPARABLE = the idea of SOFTWARE and the general-purpose computer, on paper a decade before the electronics (von Neumann turned it into the stored-program architecture every computer still runs). ⚑ THE HALTING PROBLEM: no program H can decide for ALL programs whether they halt — proved by Gödel's diagonal made mechanical (build D that does the OPPOSITE of H's prediction about D(D) → H is always wrong → H can't exist). LIVE: (1) a RUNNING Turing machine — step/run a 3-state BUSY BEAVER (halts after writing 6 ones; its growth is literally uncomputable) or a BINARY INCREMENTER (7→8), with the head crawling the tape, live state/step/ones counters, and the active rule lighting up in the table (verified); (2) the HALTING DIAGONAL — pick H's prediction, watch D refute it on BOTH branches (verified contradiction either way). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the machine, universality, undecidability of halting — rigorous, foundational, the literal blueprint of the computer) / A-MODEL-NOT-THE-BRAIN (the Church–Turing thesis — this captures ALL effective computation — is overwhelmingly supported but a THESIS about an informal notion, not a theorem; 'machines can think' was his 1950 CONJECTURE/TEST, not proven) / OFTEN-MISREAD (⚠ 'undecidable' = no SINGLE method for EVERY case, NOT 'computers are weak'; the Turing test is a thought experiment, not a verdict on consciousness). ⚑ THE LOOP CLOSES: every processor in [[psephos-processors-domain]] IS a physical Turing machine; Leibniz's calculation → Boole's algebra → Gödel's ceiling → Turing's universal machine. ⚠ HONEST — THE MAN: his Bletchley Park Bombe broke German naval Enigma (credited with shortening WWII, saving many lives), kept secret for decades so he was never publicly honoured in life; in 1952, prosecuted under Britain's gross-indecency law for being gay, forced to choose prison or chemical castration (chose the hormone treatment, lost his clearance), dead of cyanide poisoning at 41 in 1954 (ruled suicide). UK apology 2009, royal pardon 2013, the 'Alan Turing law' pardoned thousands more. The man who defined the machine and helped win the war with one was destroyed by the state he saved — the logic stands, the injustice is named. [[kurt-godel]] ← · next → Claude Shannon (the gate, the closer).

enter ↗code
CLAUDE SHANNON · XII · THE CLOSER
the gate — Boolean algebra IS the algebra of switches (1937); founder of information theory & the bit (1948)

CLAUDE SHANNON (1916–2001) — LOGIKĒ XII, THE CLOSER, where 2,500 years of logic lands on the switch. Boole made logic an algebra of 0/1; eighty years on a 21-year-old MIT student wrote what's been called the most important master's thesis ever, and it was one devastating observation: ⚑ A SWITCH IS A BIT. An electrical switch is open(0)/closed(1); two in SERIES conduct iff both closed = AND; two in PARALLEL conduct iff either closed = OR; a broken switch = NOT — so Boole's algebra of thought IS LITERALLY the algebra of circuits ('A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits', 1937). That means any logical function can be BUILT from switches and, crucially, MINIMISED by algebra into fewer parts = the birth of the LOGIC GATE & all digital design. A decade later he did it again: ⚑ INFORMATION THEORY ('A Mathematical Theory of Communication', 1948) — he gave information a precise measure (ENTROPY H=−Σp·log₂p) and named the BIT, fixing the hard floor on compression & the ceiling on channel capacity. LIVE: (1) a SWITCHING CIRCUIT — toggle switches A/B, pick series(AND)/parallel(OR)/invert(NOT), the SVG lamp lights iff current flows + the Boolean expression & truth table update (verified); (2) an EXACT BOOLEAN MINIMISER — click a truth table's outputs to define any F(A,B), watch naïve sum-of-products vs the algebra-minimal form, gate count falling (A·B+A·B̄=A; OR 3→2 terms — and HONEST when it can't, e.g. XOR stays 2; exact-cover verified); (3) an ENTROPY METER — drag a coin's bias p → H(p) bits, max 1 at p=½, 0 at certainty (verified H(0.5)=1, H(0.25)=0.811). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (switching algebra & information theory — rigorous, foundational, between them they define how every computer computes & every channel communicates) / BUILT-ON-BOOLE (the 1937 algebra is BOOLE's — Shannon's genius was the BRIDGE, seeing it IS switching; the 1948 theory he built near-from-scratch) / 'BIT'-HAS-LIMITS (⚠ Shannon information = uncertainty/message-length, NOT meaning/truth/worth — a page of noise has high entropy & no sense; reading the everyday word into the equation is the classic error). The man: a playful tinkerer — juggling machines, a maze-solving mechanical mouse, a rocket-powered frisbee, unicycling the Bell Labs halls — who treated genius as recreation. ⚑ THE LOOP CLOSES — Thales' first proof → Aristotle → Euclid → Chrysippus → Llull → Leibniz → Boole → De Morgan → Frege → Gödel → Turing → SHANNON: the algebra of thought, made physical by Shannon, now runs a billion times a second on every chip — LOGIKĒ flows out here into [[psephos-processors-domain]], the processors. The lineage is complete. [[alan-turing]] ← · LOGIKĒ complete: Thales → … → the gate.

enter ↗code
CHARLES SANDERS PEIRCE · XIII
the foundations rank — one sign builds all logic (NOR, the ampheck); the logic of relations & quantifiers Σ/Π

CHARLES SANDERS PEIRCE (1839–1914) — LOGIKĒ XIII, the great American original, by many lights the most powerful logician between Aristotle and Gödel, robbed of credit by his own neglect. TWO of his firsts sit at this lineage's heart. ⚑ FUNCTIONAL COMPLETENESS: a SINGLE connective suffices for all of logic — his 'ampheck', the arrow ↓ (today's NOR) — stated 1880, THREE DECADES before Sheffer's stroke; the deep reason a chip is one gate tiled billions of times. ⚑ RELATIONS & QUANTIFIERS: independently of Frege (1883–85) he built predicate logic and coined the notation the world still uses — Σ for 'there exists' (a logical sum), Π for 'for all' (a logical product). LIVE: (1) NOR-universality — toggle A/B, watch NOT/AND/OR built from NOTHING BUT the arrow ↓, each reproducing its standard truth table (verified 10 / 0001 / 0111); (2) Σ/Π relations — a clickable R(x,y) matrix where Σx Πy ('one x relates to every y') ≠ Πy Σx ('each y has some x'), the quantifier-order distinction at the root of all mathematics (verified). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (NOR-completeness, relations, the Σ/Π notation — rigorous, foundational, genuinely his and often EARLIEST) / ECLIPSED (published little & obscurely, much left in unread manuscripts; Frege/Russell/Sheffer got the glory for things he'd done — largely self-inflicted) / SPRAWLING (⚠ a whole cosmos beyond logic — pragmatism, semiotics, metaphysics, geodesy — much unfinished & contested). The man: lost his one professorship (Johns Hopkins) to a chaotic personal life, fell after 1891 into deepening poverty, spent his last years cold & hungry in rural Pennsylvania writing thousands of unread pages, kept alive by quiet help from William James — the arrow that builds every gate and the Σ/Π in every textbook recognised only long after he was gone. ⚑ Belongs beside [[george-boole]] & [[gottlob-frege]] in the spine; the lineage met him late, as the world did. [[claude-shannon]] ← · next → Cantor.

enter ↗code
GEORG CANTOR · XIV
the foundations rank — the infinite has sizes; the diagonal argument (the seed of Gödel & Turing)

GEORG CANTOR (1845–1918) — LOGIKĒ XIV, who proved infinity has STRUCTURE. Before him, infinity was one undifferentiated endlessness; he showed there are DIFFERENT SIZES. The counting numbers 1,2,3… are the smallest infinity (ℵ₀); the REAL NUMBERS form a strictly LARGER one that no list can ever enumerate — UNCOUNTABLE. ⚑ THE DIAGONAL ARGUMENT (1891): assume you could list all infinite binary sequences; walk the DIAGONAL (row1's 1st bit, row2's 2nd, …) and FLIP each — the result differs from every row at its own diagonal cell, so it's in no row → no list is complete → the reals are uncountable. ⚑ That exact move is the seed [[kurt-godel]] grew into incompleteness ('this statement is unprovable') and [[alan-turing]] into the halting problem ('this program loops') — ONE idea, three theorems. LIVE: (1) run the diagonal on a shuffleable list — flip the diagonal, watch the new sequence D differ from every row & sit outside the list (verified D≠row i at index i, D∉list); (2) the two infinities ℵ₀ vs 2^ℵ₀ + the endless tower (Cantor's theorem: the power set is always strictly larger). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (set theory, uncountability, the hierarchy of infinities — airtight, foundational, the ground modern math stands on) / FOUGHT-IN-LIFE (⚠ Kronecker called it humbug & blocked his career; set theory was called a 'disease'; Cantor suffered recurring breakdowns, died malnourished in a 1918 sanatorium, still disputed — Hilbert: 'no one shall expel us from the paradise Cantor created') / THE-OPEN-DOOR (his CONTINUUM HYPOTHESIS — is there a size between ℵ₀ and the reals? — turned out UNDECIDABLE: Gödel 1940 + Cohen 1963 proved it can be neither proved nor disproved from the standard axioms, the first great independence result). [[charles-peirce]] ← · next → Russell.

enter ↗code
BERTRAND RUSSELL · XV
the foundations rank — the paradox that broke Frege (1902); the theory of types = every language's type system

BERTRAND RUSSELL (1872–1970) — LOGIKĒ XV. In June 1902 a short letter to Frege ended an era. Frege built arithmetic on 'any property defines a set'; Russell asked about ONE property — 'is NOT a member of itself' — and the edifice collapsed. ⚑ RUSSELL'S PARADOX: let R = the set of all sets that don't contain themselves; then R ∈ R ⟺ R ∉ R, a flat contradiction (the village barber who shaves exactly those who don't shave themselves — who shaves him?). ⚑ THE REPAIR — THE THEORY OF TYPES: stratify everything into LEVELS (individuals at type 0, sets of them at type 1, …) with the rule x ∈ y is well-formed only when type(x)=type(y)−1, so a set can NEVER contain itself and 'R ∈ R' isn't even a legal sentence. That stratifying idea is now the TYPE SYSTEM inside every serious programming language. With Whitehead he wrote PRINCIPIA MATHEMATICA (1910–13), deriving arithmetic from logic ('1+1=2' proved well past page 360). LIVE: (1) the paradox — click either branch (R∈R or R∉R), both slam into R∈R⟺R∉R; (2) a TYPE-CHECKER — pick type(x), type(y); membership lights green iff type(x)=type(y)−1, and 'R ∈ R' (x=y) is rejected as a TYPE ERROR (verified). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the paradox is a real exact contradiction; types are a sound fix whose descendants — typed languages, proof assistants, Curry–Howard — are everywhere) / LOGICISM-FELL-SHORT (Principia needed axioms — infinity, reducibility — that aren't pure logic, and [[kurt-godel]] 1931 showed no such system can be complete; math-from-logic-alone was not achieved) / FAR-BEYOND-LOGIC (⚠ most of his 97 years were elsewhere — pacifist jailed in WWI, anti-nuclear campaigner into his 90s, Nobel laureate in LITERATURE 1950; brilliant, combative, often confidently wrong, some social views best read critically for their era). [[georg-cantor]] ← · next → Church.

enter ↗code
ALONZO CHURCH · XVI
the foundations rank — the λ-calculus: computation as pure substitution; = the Turing machine; root of all functional programming

ALONZO CHURCH (1903–1995) — LOGIKĒ XVI, who reached Turing's frontier from the opposite side. The same year Turing imagined his machine, Church defined a language with only THREE things — variables, MAKING a function (λx. …), and APPLYING one — and showed that by the single rule of SUBSTITUTION (beta-reduction) it can encode booleans, numbers, everything, and compute anything computable. ⚑ THE λ-CALCULUS (1936): no numbers or booleans built in, yet a boolean is just a chooser (TRUE=λx.λy.x, FALSE=λx.λy.y) and a number is 'apply f n times' (2=λf.λx.f(f x)); it is EXACTLY as powerful as a Turing machine, and the direct ancestor of ALL functional programming — Lisp, ML, Haskell, the λ in Python. ⚑ CHURCH'S THEOREM: independently of Turing he proved FIRST-ORDER LOGIC is UNDECIDABLE — Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem ('is there a procedure for all of logic?') answered NO. LIVE: a working λ-EVALUATOR — pick AND/OR/NOT on Church booleans or SUCC/+/× on Church numerals, watch them beta-reduce to normal form with no primitives used (verified AND T F=FALSE, 2+3=5, 2×3=6). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the λ-calculus is a complete model of computation, its equivalence to Turing machines is a theorem, undecidability of FOL is proved) / A-THESIS-NOT-A-PROOF (⚠ equivalence is provable, but the CHURCH–TURING THESIS — this captures ALL effective computation — concerns an informal notion & can't be formally proved, though every model ever built collapses to the same class) / SHARED-SPOTLIGHT (Church proved undecidability just before Turing, but the vivid MACHINE took the public credit; the abstract λ waited decades for programming to make it obvious). ⚑ TWO ROADS, ONE EDGE: machine = the HARDWARE picture ([[psephos-processors-domain]]); λ = the SOFTWARE picture (functional programming + the types from [[bertrand-russell]]) — logic forks here into the two halves of CS. The man: monkish precision (multiple ink colors, erased never crossed out), a MAKER OF MAKERS — advised Turing's PhD at Princeton, plus Kleene & Rosser, founded the Journal of Symbolic Logic. ⚑ machine + function = the two definitions of the computable. [[bertrand-russell]] ← · next → David Hilbert.

enter ↗code
DAVID HILBERT · XVII
the foundations rank — the program the whole crisis answered; the 23 problems; Hilbert's infinite Hotel

DAVID HILBERT (1862–1943) — LOGIKĒ XVII, the FINAL BOSS of this domain: nearly every result here was an answer to a question HE posed. The towering mathematician of his age set the 20th century's agenda with the 23 PROBLEMS (1900) and dreamed the boldest dream in logic — ⚑ HILBERT'S PROGRAM: prove all mathematics COMPLETE (every truth provable) + CONSISTENT (no contradictions) + DECIDABLE (a mechanical procedure settles any statement), by safe finitary reasoning. ⚑ THE ANSWER it received: [[kurt-godel]] 1931 killed completeness & self-proved consistency; [[alonzo-church]] & [[alan-turing]] 1936 killed decidability (the Entscheidungsproblem) — and to prove 'no machine decides all math' they had to DEFINE what a machine is = the computer. His program failed more productively than almost anything has succeeded; the failure IS the foundation of [[psephos-processors-domain]]. LIVE: HILBERT'S HOTEL — a hotel with infinitely many rooms, all full, that still takes more guests: one new guest → everyone shifts n→n+1, room 0 opens (nobody evicted); an infinite bus → everyone moves n→2n, every ODD room opens (verified mappings) — Cantor's infinity made playable. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the axiomatic method, the 23 problems, Grundlagen der Geometrie fixing Euclid's gaps, Hilbert spaces in quantum mechanics — monumental, shaped all modern math & physics) / THE-PROGRAM-FAILED (⚠ his SPECIFIC dream was proven impossible — math can't be complete+consistent+decidable — but the failure BIRTHED computability theory) / 'WE-WILL-KNOW'-NOT-ALL (his epitaph 'Wir müssen wissen, wir werden wissen' promises no unknowables; there ARE true-but-unprovable & undecidable statements — the quest for total knowledge was unreachable and built CS on the way). The man: led Göttingen, the world's math center, and watched the Nazis DESTROY it after 1933 (purging his Jewish colleagues — asked if math at Göttingen suffered from 'the departure of the Jews': 'Suffered? It doesn't exist any longer'); died 1943 in the emptied city. [[alonzo-church]] ← · next → Łukasiewicz.

enter ↗code
JAN ŁUKASIEWICZ · XVIII
the foundations rank — a THIRD truth value (many-valued logic); Polish notation (→ RPN, every parser)

JAN ŁUKASIEWICZ (1878–1956) — LOGIKĒ XVIII, who broke the 2,300-year monopoly of true/false. Aristotle's EXCLUDED MIDDLE says every statement is true or false; Łukasiewicz asked about the OPEN FUTURE ('there will be a sea-battle tomorrow' — neither true nor false YET) and in 1920 built the first rigorous ⚑ THREE-VALUED LOGIC: a third value ½ ('possible'/undetermined) between 0 and 1 — founding ALL many-valued & FUZZY logic (degrees of truth, now in control systems & AI). ⚑ POLISH NOTATION: operators BEFORE operands, no parentheses needed ('+ 2 × 3 4'); its reverse RPN is how calculators, the language Forth, stack machines, and every compiler's expression parser actually compute. LIVE: (1) 3-valued logic Ł3 — set P,Q ∈ {0,½,1}, watch ¬∧∨→ (¬a=1−a, ∧=min, ∨=max, a→b=min(1,1−a+b)) and the EXCLUDED MIDDLE P∨¬P come out ½ (not 1!) when P=½ — bivalence visibly fails (verified); (2) a working PREFIX evaluator ('+ 2 * 3 4' = 14, verified). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (many-valued logic & Polish notation are real, rigorous, and everywhere — fuzzy/quantum/probabilistic logic & every parser) / A-CHOICE-NOT-THE-LAW (⚠ dropping bivalence is a deliberate CHOICE of logic for certain problems, NOT a proof classical logic is wrong; whether the future is 'really' ½ is philosophy) / A-COMPLICATED-LIFE (⚠ a giant of the Lwów–Warsaw school & briefly Poland's education minister; his path through WWII is contested historical discussion — this renders the mathematics, which stands on its own, and does not litigate the biography). [[david-hilbert]] ← · next → Tarski.

enter ↗code
ALFRED TARSKI · XIX
the foundations rank — the definition of TRUTH (model theory); truth is undefinable within its own language

ALFRED TARSKI (1901–1983) — LOGIKĒ XIX. 'True' is logic's most-used word, and before Tarski no one had said precisely what it MEANS without circularity or paradox. In 1933 he pinned it down: ⚑ SEMANTIC TRUTH — a sentence is true exactly when it FITS the structure it describes; 'snow is white' is true IFF snow is white (Convention T); a formula's truth is always RELATIVE TO A MODEL. This founded MODEL THEORY (half of modern logic; the semantics under database queries, formal verification, program correctness). ⚑ THE UNDEFINABILITY THEOREM (a semantic sibling of [[kurt-godel]]): no sufficiently rich language can define its OWN truth predicate → 'true' must live in a higher METALANGUAGE → which is exactly why the LIAR paradox dissolves (stratify object-language vs metalanguage and the self-referential sentence can't be formed — same cure as [[bertrand-russell]]'s types). LIVE: (1) truth-in-a-model — toggle atoms p,q,r, evaluate φ=(p∧q)→r, and see the SAME sentence true in one preset model and false in another (verified M₁ false, M₂ true); (2) the Liar — both branches spin forever in one language, resolved by the object/metalanguage split. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (semantic truth & model theory — rigorous, foundational, the basis of logical consequence & computing semantics) / TRUTH-IS-LANGUAGE-RELATIVE (⚠ defined for FORMAL languages, relative to a model & metalanguage — a precise mathematical relation, NOT a theory of Truth-about-reality) / THE-'PARADOX'-ISN'T-PHYSICS (⚠ Banach–Tarski: a ball → two balls is a real theorem about IDEALIZED point-sets needing the Axiom of Choice & non-measurable pieces with no volume — says nothing about cutting real matter; pop 'duplication machine' accounts are wrong). The man: a Polish Jew lecturing in the USA in Sept 1939 when Germany invaded — the trip saved his life though much of his family was murdered in the Holocaust; became the great founder of logic at Berkeley. ⚑ With Tarski the foundations rank rests: from [[thales-of-miletus]]' first proof through the gate, the limits, and the meaning of truth itself. [[jan-lukasiewicz]] ← · next → THE OTHER HALF (the women of the lineage).

enter ↗code
ADA LOVELACE · XX
the other half — the first algorithm (Note G, 1843); the leap that a machine is a symbol-machine

ADA LOVELACE (1815–1852) — LOGIKĒ XX, where THE OTHER HALF begins, at the summit. ⚖ THE HONEST FRAME: nineteen spheres of this lineage were men — not because women couldn't reason, but because for millennia they were FORBIDDEN THE ROOM (barred from universities, denied degrees, lecturing under men's names). The women here did first-rank logic THROUGH walls built to keep them out; the scarcity is the injustice, not the measure of their minds. Ada is the face of UD0 ('the ancestry of the algorithm, after Ada Lovelace') and earns it: in her 1843 NOTES on Babbage's Analytical Engine (3× the length of the paper she translated), ⚑ NOTE G lays out a complete step-by-step procedure — with a LOOP and stored VARIABLES — for the machine to compute the BERNOULLI NUMBERS: the first algorithm ever published for a machine. ⚑ THE LEAP no one else made: that a machine manipulating numbers could manipulate ANY symbols — music, logic, language — 'the science of operations' = the idea of the GENERAL-PURPOSE COMPUTER, a century early. LIVE: (1) run Note G — the engine computes the Bernoulli numbers EXACTLY as fractions (BigInt rationals via the recurrence ΣC(n+1,k)Bₖ=0; verified B₂=1/6, B₄=−1/30, B₆=1/42, B₈=−1/30); (2) the symbol-machine (numbers→music→logic→letters). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (Note G is a genuine complete algorithm; the symbol-machine insight is the conceptual seed of general-purpose computing) / 'FIRST PROGRAMMER'-DEBATED (⚠ Babbage built the engine & sketched earlier routines; how much of Note G is hers is argued — but the Notes & the visionary leap are firmly hers) / A-MACHINE-NEVER-BUILT (the engine wasn't completed in her life; her code ran on paper for a century — and she warned it 'has no pretensions to originate anything', a caution AI still needs). Byron's daughter, who fused poetry & math into 'poetical science'; died of cancer at 36, her father's age. [[alfred-tarski]] ← · next → Christine Ladd-Franklin.

enter ↗code
CHRISTINE LADD-FRANKLIN · XXI
the other half — the antilogism: one test for every syllogism; the degree withheld 44 years

CHRISTINE LADD-FRANKLIN (1847–1930) — LOGIKĒ XXI, Peirce's student who found the SINGLE test that unifies Aristotle's whole syllogistic. ⚑ THE ANTILOGISM: a syllogism is valid exactly when its two premises plus the CONTRADICTORY of its conclusion form an INCONSISTENT TRIAD (three statements that can't all be true) — and the symmetry is the prize: one inconsistent triad yields THREE valid syllogisms (drop any one, negate it, conclude from the other two). It was for decades the cleanest decision procedure for the syllogism. LIVE: (1) an antilogism validity tester — pick a syllogism, watch its antilogism checked for inconsistency by full Venn-region enumeration → VALID/INVALID (verified Barbara/Celarent/Darii valid, undistributed-middle invalid); (2) one inconsistency → three syllogisms (clickable). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the antilogism is a correct, elegant, unifying decision procedure for the categorical syllogism — praised by Peirce, taught for generations) / ONE-PIECE-OF-A-FIELD (the classical syllogism, not the full predicate logic [[gottlob-frege]] was building) / ⚠ THE-DEGREE-WITHHELD (she completed EVERY requirement for a Johns Hopkins PhD in 1882 — admitted only because Sylvester intervened, on condition her name not appear in the register — and the university REFUSED the degree because she was a woman; finally granted it in 1926, forty-four years later, at 78). Also did major work on colour vision. ⚑ The four-decade delay is the plainest illustration of why this lineage was, for nineteen spheres, all men. [[ada-lovelace]] ← · next → Rózsa Péter.

enter ↗code
RÓZSA PÉTER · XXII
the other half — founder of recursion theory; a function that outruns every bounded loop

RÓZSA PÉTER (1905–1977) — LOGIKĒ XXII, founder of RECURSION THEORY as a subject (her 1951 'Recursive Functions' was the first systematic treatment) — the mathematics of functions defined in terms of themselves, the formal heart of computability alongside Gödel/Church/Turing. ⚑ THE ACKERMANN–PÉTER FUNCTION: she gave the Ackermann function its standard 2-variable form (A(0,n)=n+1; A(m,0)=A(m−1,1); A(m,n)=A(m−1,A(m,n−1))) — TOTAL and COMPUTABLE yet growing so explosively it provably ESCAPES primitive recursion, proving 'bounded loops ≠ all computation'. LIVE: (1) run the Ackermann–Péter function & watch it explode with the recursive-call count (verified A(2,2)=7, A(3,3)=61; A(4,2) already 19,729 digits); (2) primitive recursion building add & mult from the successor. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (recursion theory systematised; the 2-variable Ackermann form is a textbook total-but-not-primitive-recursive function) / SHARED-ROOTS (the original function is Ackermann's 1928; she simplified/generalised it & built the surrounding field, with Gödel/Kleene in its parentage) / ⚠ SURVIVED-TO-BUILD-IT (a Hungarian Jew dismissed from teaching under the fascist laws & confined to the BUDAPEST GHETTO — she did & preserved the mathematics through it; later wrote 'Playing with Infinity', insisting math is for everyone). [[christine-ladd-franklin]] ← · next → Julia Robinson.

enter ↗code
JULIA ROBINSON · XXIII
the other half — Hilbert's 10th: no algorithm decides if a Diophantine equation has integer solutions

JULIA ROBINSON (1919–1985) — LOGIKĒ XXIII, who spent decades on [[david-hilbert]]'s TENTH PROBLEM: is there an algorithm deciding whether any DIOPHANTINE (integer polynomial) equation has integer solutions? She built the keystone machinery — the ROBINSON HYPOTHESIS and the Davis–Putnam–Robinson theorem — that Yuri Matiyasevich completed in 1970, proving the answer is NO. ⚑ THE MRDP THEOREM: Diophantine sets are EXACTLY the computably-enumerable sets → the integers are Turing-complete → since some c.e. sets are undecidable ([[alan-turing]]), so is Diophantine solvability — Hilbert's 10th is UNDECIDABLE. A stunning unification: number theory IS computability. LIVE: a Diophantine solution-hunter (bounded integer search over Pell & other equations — finds solutions where they exist, verified x²−2y²=1 → (1,0),(3,2),(17,12)…; and the asymmetry — search confirms 'yes', never 'no' — that IS the undecidability wall). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (MRDP settles a 70-year problem; rigorous & deep) / A-RELAY-NOT-A-SOLO (honest name MRDP = Matiyasevich–Robinson–Davis–Putnam; her hypothesis was the keystone the edifice waited a decade on; the young Matiyasevich added the final Fibonacci step — she generously credited him & they became friends across the Cold War) / THE-SEARCH-CAN'T-DECIDE (a finite hunt can't prove 'no solutions exist'). 1st woman president of the AMS & 1st woman mathematician in the National Academy; weakened for life by childhood rheumatic fever; 'remember me for the theorems I have proved.' [[rozsa-peter]] ← · next → Ruth Barcan Marcus.

enter ↗code
RUTH BARCAN MARCUS · XXIV · THE OTHER HALF CLOSES
the other half — the first quantified modal logic (1946) & the Barcan formula ∀x□Fx → □∀xFx

RUTH BARCAN MARCUS (1921–2012) — LOGIKĒ XXIV, who at TWENTY-FIVE first rigorously combined the two great extensions of logic — QUANTIFIERS (∀/∃, [[gottlob-frege]]) and MODALITY (necessity □ / possibility ◇) — into the first systems of ⚑ QUANTIFIED MODAL LOGIC (1946), and asked the question their union forces: does ORDER matter? ⚑ THE BARCAN FORMULA: ∀x□Fx → □∀xFx — the principle governing how necessity and 'for all' slide past each other, written a DECADE before the possible-worlds semantics that would explain it. She also pioneered DIRECT REFERENCE (names as bare 'tags' picking the same object in every world), anticipating Kripke by ~15 years. LIVE: a possible-worlds model — set F per world×individual; ∀x□Fx ↔ □∀xFx always agree (the Barcan formula holds in constant domains), while ◇∀xFx vs ∀x◇Fx can SPLIT (order matters), verified. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the first quantified modal logic & the eponymous formula — foundational; modal logic underlies the semantics of necessity, time, knowledge, obligation, program verification) / SEMANTICS-CAME-LATER (she gave the axiomatics; the possible-worlds interpretation was filled in by Kripke & others in the late 1950s–60s) / ⚠ PRIORITY-SHE-HAD-TO-DEFEND (her ideas on direct reference & the necessity of identity were later credited to men — a documented dispute, incl. a notorious seminar exchange — the record now resolves in her favour). Published this in the 1940s when the profession barely admitted women, raised four children, became the first woman to chair Yale philosophy. ⚑ With her THE OTHER HALF stands — [[ada-lovelace]]·[[christine-ladd-franklin]]·[[rozsa-peter]]·[[julia-robinson]]·Barcan Marcus, first-rank logic done through walls. [[julia-robinson]] ← · next → Emmy Noether.

enter ↗code
EMMY NOETHER · XXV
the other half — the algebra of STRUCTURE (groups/rings/ideals); 'the most important woman in math' (Einstein)

EMMY NOETHER (1882–1935) — LOGIKĒ XXV, the greatest woman mathematician in history (Einstein: 'the most significant creative mathematical genius thus far produced since the higher education of women began'). [[george-boole]] made LOGIC an algebra; Noether changed what ALGEBRA IS. ⚑ THE STRUCTURAL TURN: before her, algebra = calculating with particular numbers/polynomials/matrices; she lifted it to reason about ABSTRACT STRUCTURES — a group, a ring, an ideal — defined by AXIOMS ALONE, caring only about the rules an operation obeys, never what the elements 'really are'. That IS modern mathematics, and the exact way modern logic treats its own objects (Boolean ALGEBRAS, lattices, models) — Boolean algebra is just one structure in a vast family. ⚑ NOETHER'S THEOREM (1918): every continuous symmetry yields a conservation law (time-symmetry→energy, space→momentum) — a pillar of physics. LIVE: a Cayley-table explorer — pick a group (ℤ₄ clock arithmetic, the logic values {0,1} under XOR, the Klein four-group, S₃ triangle symmetries), the four axioms (closure/associativity/identity/inverses) checked live (verified ℤ₄ is a group, a broken table fails associativity); wildly different things are the SAME structure when their tables match. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (Noetherian rings, her treatment of ideals, Noether's theorem — permanent fixtures of math & physics) / ALGEBRA-NOT-'LOGIC'-NARROWLY (she's the supreme ALGEBRAIST, not a formal logician — but the axiomatic-structural method she perfected is the ground modern logic stands on, which earns her place here) / ⚠ BARRED-THEN-EXPELLED (denied a paid post for being a woman, she lectured for YEARS under HILBERT's name on the timetable — Hilbert: the senate 'is not a bathhouse'; in 1933 the Nazis expelled her, a Jew, from Göttingen; she fled to Bryn Mawr & died in 1935 at 53 after surgery). Her methods, she said, 'crept in everywhere anonymously' — the structural language of all modern math. [[ruth-barcan-marcus]] ← · next → Stephen Kleene.

enter ↗code
STEPHEN KLEENE · XXVI
the other half (men) — regular expressions = finite automata; the Kleene star *

STEPHEN KLEENE (1909–1994) — LOGIKĒ XXVI, [[alonzo-church]]'s student & a founder of recursion theory, who gave one of its pieces a form you use daily. ⚑ KLEENE'S THEOREM (1951): the patterns you can write with a REGULAR EXPRESSION — built from characters by three operations, CONCATENATION, CHOICE (|), and REPETITION (the *) — are EXACTLY the patterns a FINITE-STATE MACHINE can recognize. Two utterly different descriptions (an algebra of patterns vs a machine with a few states) define the same languages — the regular languages. The repetition operator is the ⚑ KLEENE STAR (*), named for him (also the Kleene closure & the recursion theorem), running inside every grep, lexer, search box & validator on Earth. LIVE: a real regular-expression matcher (concatenation · union | · the star *; verified (a|b)*c matches 'ababc', rejects 'abab'; a*b matches 'aaab') + a batch view + Kleene's bridge regex⇄automata. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (Kleene's theorem is a CS cornerstone; the star/closure/recursion theorem are permanent tools) / A-LIMITED-CLASS (regular languages are the WEAKEST rung — finite memory, can't count unboundedly / match balanced parens; that limit IS the characterization of bounded memory) / ⚠ 'REGEX'≠REGULAR (modern regex engines add backreferences/lookahead that EXCEED true regular expressions & run slower; Kleene's are the clean mathematical core). The * is among the most-typed mathematical inventions in history. [[emmy-noether]] ← · next → Gerhard Gentzen.

enter ↗code
GERHARD GENTZEN · XXVII
the other half (men) — natural deduction & the sequent calculus; cut-elimination; proofs = programs

GERHARD GENTZEN (1909–1945) — LOGIKĒ XXVII, who found the structure of PROOF ITSELF. Frege & Russell could write proofs, but in unnatural axiom-chains; in 1934 Gentzen built the system matching real reasoning — ⚑ NATURAL DEDUCTION: each connective gets an INTRODUCTION rule (how to prove it) and an ELIMINATION rule (how to use it), reasoning from ASSUMPTIONS you later DISCHARGE (→I = assume A, derive B, conclude A→B; →E = modus ponens, [[chrysippus]]). He also gave the SEQUENT CALCULUS and ⚑ THE HAUPTSATZ (cut-elimination): any proof using a lemma can be rewritten lemma-free — proofs always NORMALIZE. ⚑ CURRY–HOWARD: intro/elim rules match how you build & use data → a proof of A→B IS a function, normalizing a proof IS running a program ([[bertrand-russell]]'s types made to work; the basis of every proof assistant). LIVE: a natural-deduction proof builder — pick a theorem (A→A, modus ponens, A∧B→B∧A, A→(B→A)), apply intro/elim rules in order, each step checked, the goal-line lights up. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (natural deduction, the sequent calculus, cut-elimination — rigorous, foundational, the basis of proof theory & proof assistants) / CONSISTENCY-WITH-A-PRICE (his 1936 consistency proof for arithmetic uses transfinite induction up to ε₀, a resource OUTSIDE arithmetic — it doesn't evade [[kurt-godel]], it MEASURES what consistency costs, founding ordinal proof theory) / ⚠ A-DARK-BIOGRAPHY (stated without softening: Gentzen JOINED THE NAZI PARTY & the SA and worked within institutions purging his Jewish colleagues; he died in 1945 in a Soviet-administered Prague internment camp at 35 of malnutrition — the logic is his, so is the record; the work doesn't absolve the life, the life doesn't erase the work). [[stephen-kleene]] ← · next → Saul Kripke.

enter ↗code
SAUL KRIPKE · XXVIII
the other half (men) — possible-worlds semantics: the meaning behind Barcan Marcus's modal logic

SAUL KRIPKE (1940–2022) — LOGIKĒ XXVIII, who as a TEENAGER gave modal logic its MEANING. [[ruth-barcan-marcus]] gave the axioms; Kripke gave the model: ⚑ POSSIBLE-WORLDS SEMANTICS — a set of WORLDS connected by an ACCESSIBILITY relation; □P ('necessarily P') is true at a world iff P holds in EVERY world it can see, ◇P iff in SOME. The astonishing part: the SHAPE of accessibility decides which logic you get — REFLEXIVE validates □p→p (system T), add TRANSITIVE for S4, an EQUIVALENCE for S5. LIVE: a 3-world Kripke model (SVG graph) — toggle p per world, switch the accessibility frame, evaluate □p/◇p at a world, and watch the modal axioms T/4/B/S5 switch on as the relation's properties (reflexive/transitive/symmetric) hold (verified). ⚑ This colonised half of logic & CS: worlds as MOMENTS = temporal logic (verify a chip never reaches a bad state); accessibility as 'compatible with what's known' = epistemic logic (knowledge in AI/economics); as 'provable' = [[kurt-godel]] in modal dress — model checkers are walking Kripke structures. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (possible-worlds semantics with soundness/completeness linking frames to systems — the standard model everywhere from philosophy to formal verification, produced as a teenager ~1959–63) / SEMANTICS-ATOP-HER-SYNTAX (⚠ the quantified-modal SYSTEMS & the Barcan formula are [[ruth-barcan-marcus]]'s 1946; even 'rigid designators' was her 'tags' idea first; Kripke supplied the SEMANTICS — a major, largely independent achievement, but it's Barcan's syntax + Kripke's semantics, and there was a sharp documented priority dispute) / 'WORLDS'-A-MODEL-NOT-METAPHYSICS (the possible worlds are a mathematical device — whether other worlds 'really exist' is separate philosophy; Kripke was cautious). ⚑ With Kripke the modal thread [[ruth-barcan-marcus]] opened is complete — the syntax, and the worlds that give it meaning. [[gerhard-gentzen]] ←.

enter ↗code
HASKELL CURRY
the modern foundations — combinatory logic (compute with NO variables); Curry–Howard (proofs = programs)

HASKELL CURRY (1900–1982) — LOGIKĒ, the modern foundations; the λ in 'Haskell' is named for him. [[alonzo-church]]'s λ-calculus binds variables (which get captured, renamed, tangled); Curry asked — can you compute with NO variables at all? ⚑ COMBINATORY LOGIC: three fixed operators — I (do nothing), K (keep the first, drop the second), S (share an argument between two functions) — and that's the whole machine; no x, no λ, just combinators copying/deleting/rearranging arguments, EXACTLY as powerful as the λ-calculus & Turing machine. ⚑ CURRY–HOWARD CORRESPONDENCE: the type of K is the logic axiom A→(B→A), the type of S is (A→(B→C))→((A→B)→(A→C)) — so PROPOSITIONS ARE TYPES, PROOFS ARE PROGRAMS, normalising a proof IS running a program. LIVE: a combinator reducer (I x→x; K x y→x; S x y z→x z (y z)) — verified S K K behaves as the identity I, variable-free. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (combinatory logic = a complete variable-free model of computation = the λ-calculus; Curry–Howard is one of the deepest unifications in logic & CS) / SHARED-CREDIT (⚠ the combinators came first from Schönfinkel 1924; 'Curry–Howard' = Curry's observation + William Howard's 1969 formalisation) / A-PARADOX-TOO (Curry's paradox — untyped self-reference is dangerous). ⚑ He proved binding variables is a CONVENIENCE not a necessity, and found the seam where proving & programming are one cloth (the basis of every proof assistant; [[gerhard-gentzen]]'s natural deduction IS a type system). [[alonzo-church]] ← · next → Emil Post.

enter ↗code
EMIL POST
the modern foundations — production systems; the Post Correspondence Problem (undecidable dominoes)

EMIL POST (1897–1954) — LOGIKĒ, the great ALMOST-FIRST. Working alone in New York in the 1920s he reached the core of [[kurt-godel]]'s incompleteness and [[alan-turing]]'s undecidability — BEFORE either — but illness & a cautious editor kept it unpublished, and the credit went elsewhere. ⚑ PRODUCTION SYSTEMS: computation is just REWRITING STRINGS BY RULES — a model as powerful as the Turing machine, the ancestor of every formal grammar & term-rewriting system. ⚑ THE POST CORRESPONDENCE PROBLEM: given dominoes each with a top & bottom string, can you lay some in a row so the top reads the same as the bottom? Sounds like a game; it's UNDECIDABLE — no algorithm solves it in general, so it's the standard tool for proving OTHER problems undecidable. LIVE: play PCP — stack dominoes so top=bottom; a bounded solver finds short matches (verified a known solvable instance); deciding solvability in general is impossible. CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (production/rewriting systems are a complete model of computation; PCP is rigorously undecidable & the everyday undecidability tool) / THE-PRIORITY-HE-LOST (⚠ anticipated Gödel c.1921 & the Turing-machine idea but didn't publish in time; the anticipation is now acknowledged, the formal credit fairly went to those who published) / A-LIFE-OF-OBSTACLES (lost an arm at 13, severe bipolar disorder, heavy teaching load, died at 57). ⚑ [[alan-turing]]'s halting problem wearing a child's puzzle; the man who saw the limits first. [[haskell-curry]] ← · next → Wittgenstein.

enter ↗code
LUDWIG WITTGENSTEIN
the modern foundations — the Tractatus (1921): the truth table; logical truths are tautologies that say nothing

LUDWIG WITTGENSTEIN (1889–1951) — LOGIKĒ, the modern foundations; [[bertrand-russell]]'s most famous student. In the TRACTATUS LOGICO-PHILOSOPHICUS (1921) he gave the TRUTH TABLE its modern form and showed a statement's meaning is NOTHING BUT how its truth depends on its parts — and from that, that the truths of LOGIC are TAUTOLOGIES (true on EVERY row, no matter how the world is) → logic says nothing about reality, it shows the SCAFFOLDING; what can't be pictured (ethics, the mystical) lies outside what language can say ('whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent'). LIVE: a truth-table machine — build a propositional formula over p,q,r + connectives, the full table is computed and classified TAUTOLOGY / CONTRADICTION / CONTINGENT (verified p∨¬p=taut, p∧¬p=contradiction, De Morgan & the contrapositive = tautologies). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (the truth-table method is standard & correct; 'logical truths are contentless tautologies' is a genuine clarification of what logic IS — the great-grandparent of the SAT solver) / NOT-THE-SOLE-INVENTOR (⚠ truth tables appear near-simultaneously in Wittgenstein, [[emil-post]] 1921, and earlier in [[charles-peirce]]; his move was philosophical) / HE-TOOK-IT-BACK (⚠ he later REPUDIATED much of the Tractatus in the Philosophical Investigations — meaning is use, not picturing; and he's a PHILOSOPHER first). The man: a steel heir who gave away a fortune, wrote it partly in WWI trenches, quit to teach schoolchildren, then returned to demolish his own system. [[emil-post]] ← · next → George Boolos.

enter ↗code
GEORGE BOOLOS
the modern foundations — provability logic (GL): Gödel's incompleteness as a tiny modal logic

GEORGE BOOLOS (1940–1996) — LOGIKĒ, the modern foundations; the CLARIFIER. [[kurt-godel]] proved incompleteness with heavy machinery; Boolos showed it all snaps into a tiny MODAL LOGIC — read the box □ not as 'necessarily' ([[saul-kripke]]) but as 'IT IS PROVABLE THAT', and provability in arithmetic is governed by one short system, ⚑ GL, whose distinctive law is LÖB'S THEOREM □(□p→p)→□p. Incompleteness becomes a one-line modal fact: the system can't prove its own consistency, ¬□⊥ (Gödel's SECOND theorem). LIVE: the two self-referential sentences — Gödel's G↔¬□G ('I am NOT provable') is TRUE BUT UNPROVABLE, while Henkin/Löb's H↔□H ('I AM provable') is actually PROVABLE (Löb's theorem) — click each to follow its logic; the asymmetry IS incompleteness (verified). CONFIDENCE-TIERED: STRONG (provability logic GL is a precise, complete modal account of provability — Solovay; 'The Logic of Provability' 1993 is the standard text; re-derives Gödel & Löb in clean modal lines, tied to [[saul-kripke]]'s semantics) / A-REFRAMING-NOT-A-NEW-THEOREM (the core results are Gödel's & Löb's & the completeness is Solovay's; Boolos's gift was the unifying modal VIEW & unmatched exposition) / FAMOUS-FOR-PUZZLES-TOO (⚠ the 'Hardest Logic Puzzle Ever' (three gods) refines Smullyan; Gödel's 2nd in words of ONE SYLLABLE — dazzling exposition, not his deepest math). A great teacher of logic, co-author of 'Computability and Logic', a crossword champion; died of cancer at 55. ⚑ He took the hardest theorem in this lineage and handed it back as a small clean modal logic. With Boolos LOGIKĒ rests: [[thales-of-miletus]] → … → the logic of proof itself. [[ludwig-wittgenstein]] ←.

NUMBERS STATIONS (NST) — Paper VI of VI, the FINALE of the AUDIO CIPHER CHANNELS series and the one channel that carries an actual cipher: a voice reads five-digit number groups over shortwave, encrypted with a ONE-TIME PAD. The carrier is the dumbest possible channel (a human voice on a $10 radio, no auth, no signature); ALL the security lives in the pad — random digits, held physically by sender and receiver, each used once then destroyed. Shannon proved in 1949 this achieves PERFECT SECRECY: the ciphertext reveals literally zero about the plaintext without the pad — not hard to break, impossible, forever (the constraint is physical, not mathematical). The lineage (WWI Morse stations → SOE/BBC coded messages → the Cold-War peak & the Lincolnshire Poacher E03 from RAF Akrotiri ~1970s-2008 → the Conet Project 1997, 150+ recordings → the courtroom: the Cuban Five & Ana Montes, 2001). Live: real mod-10 OTP encrypt/decrypt with a fresh pad — verified round-trip + the perfect-secrecy property (same plaintext, two pads → different ciphers). ⚑ The series' architectural lesson: carrier vs cipher, perfectly separated — security as a PHYSICAL key-discipline problem (never reuse it, never let it leak / hum out / be forged), not a math one. Two-layer honest: the OTP math is exact and Shannon's proof is a theorem; the demo's pad uses Math.random (not crypto-secure) and a synth voice — the key-management that makes it unbreakable is described, not enacted. THE FILTRATION SYSTEM

THE FILTRATION SYSTEM — built ON [[duality-engine]] (imports its MACI validator): a tiered water-filter for raw multi-party logs that answers WHAT DID WE ACTUALLY DECIDE, AND WHO HAD THE AUTHORITY. Three filters, each only REMOVES or DEMOTES (never adds back), so what survives is high-confidence by construction and every removal lands in an auditable tray. FS (coarse screen): mechanical parse only — who/when/literal content + authority from the directory; drops non-messages & unknown speakers; can't be 'wrong'. FSS (forward, optimistic): generous role promotion tuned for ZERO false negatives — if a line could be a decision, tag it (over-tag on purpose). BSS (backward, skeptical): demotes the unbacked — a decision by a non-authority, an off-topic red herring, a casual non-commitment. The FSS/BSS GAP = the contested set routed to human review; what survives both = CERTIFIED. Worked example: a 20-message Slack thread choosing a cache — the contractor's UNAUTHORIZED 'im switching us to memcached' (the change that caused the 2:30 incident) is demoted (advisory cannot decide) and the certified answer is what the SOVEREIGN actually called: cache = REDIS. Mirrors the engine's converged FSS/BSS auditor, pointed at real-world provenance. Ships tiered_extractor.py + the worked example. Honest: role cues are regex heuristics, not language understanding — hence the FS foundation + the human-review tray; built to be auditable, not blindly trusted. David Lee Wise / Bridge-Burners LLC.
